source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "ដំណាំល្ហុង" (Papaya Cultivation), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
Papaya trees grown from this method typically begin producing harvestable fruit around 5–6 months after planting. The main ripeness indicator is the fruit skin starting to turn from green to yellow — farmers can pick fruit showing early yellow streaking if they want to allow further ripening off the tree, or wait for more yellow coloration for fruit intended for immediate sale or consumption.

After harvesting, handle the fruit carefully to avoid bruising, and keep harvested papaya in a cool, shaded area rather than in direct sun to preserve fruit quality until it is sold or eaten.
